meta.description: Housing market dashboard data — NYC suburban markets for home purchase research

mortgage_rates.rate_driver: Iran conflict + May CPI 3.8% — rates ticking up week-over-week
mortgage_rates.notes: 30yr at 6.51% (up from 6.50% prior week). 15yr at 5.85% (up from 5.79%). 20yr at 6.54%. Above conforming limit ($832,750) adds ~0.10-0.15% for jumbo.

primary_markets.name: Floral Park

downtown.character: Quaint mid-century main street with three commercial corridors — Covert Ave, Tulip Ave, and Jericho Turnpike. Flat, sidewalked, and friendly for daily errands with a classic Long Island village feel.
downtown.verdict: Genuinely walkable for a Long Island village — daily errands and the LIRR on foot, but nightlife variety is thin.

primary_markets.notes: Strong LIRR access; Nassau County taxes fully combined including school district.

primary_markets.name: Rockville Centre

downtown.character: The most authentically walkable downtown of the LI primary markets. North Park Avenue is a tree-lined strip dense with restaurants, bars, and boutiques — over 98 dining and drinking establishments in the village, with genuine evening foot traffic rare for Long Island.
highlights: North Park Avenue dining & bar strip
downtown.verdict: Best LI primary market downtown — rare suburb where you can leave the car home for evenings out.

primary_markets.notes: Higher tax burden than Floral Park; well-regarded school district.

primary_markets.name: Maplewood

downtown.character: One of the best downtowns in the entire NYC suburban ring. Maplewood Avenue is a dense, diverse strip with fine dining, pubs, a jazz scene, and a farmer's market — all in a 5-minute pedestrian loop connecting the train station to Memorial Park.
highlights: Maplewood Avenue village strip (train to park)
Memorial Park adjacent to village center
downtown.verdict: Car-optional for evenings, weekends, and errands — a true 'village in the suburbs' with constant foot traffic.

primary_markets.notes: Added for NJ geographic diversity and NYC spillover demand angle. Note higher NJ tax burden.

primary_markets.name: Pelham

downtown.character: Pre-automobile street grid with continuous sidewalks and the Metro-North station at the center of it all. Fifth Avenue and Wolfs Lane flank the station with independent shops, a Michelin-recognized steakhouse, and the Pelham Art Center — more cultural depth than comparably-sized LI villages.
highlights: Fifth Ave / Wolfs Lane (two-sided main street)
downtown.verdict: Genuinely walkable and well-programmed — station-centered grid is a structural advantage over car-first LI suburbs.

primary_markets.notes: Fastest commute of all markets. Metro-North to GCT is the key differentiator vs. LIRR to Penn.

research_markets.name: Rockaway Park

downtown.character: Beach community with surf-casual vibe. Rockaway Beach Blvd is the main strip with bars, cafes, and surf shops; the Atlantic Ocean boardwalk is the social center.
downtown.verdict: Seasonally walkable and charming in summer, thins out off-season. Beach-town strip rather than traditional village downtown.

research_markets.notes: Lowest taxes of all markets due to NYC Class 1 assessment structure. Flood zone risk (FEMA Zone AE) adds ~$2-4K/yr flood insurance. Schools vary widely — Scholars' Academy 9/10 but admission not guaranteed by address.

research_markets.name: Larchmont

downtown.character: Quintessential Sound Shore village with two downtown nodes — boutique shops, farm-to-table dining, and antique stores all steps from the Metro-North platform.
highlights: Manor Park waterfront on Long Island Sound
downtown.verdict: One of Westchester's most walkable downtowns. Can skip the car for daily errands — true village feel at its best.

research_markets.notes: Above $700K-$1M budget ceiling. Shares Mamaroneck UFSD (A+, #24 NY) with Town of Mamaroneck at a ~$550K premium. Fast-moving market.

research_markets.name: Bronxville

downtown.character: Deliberately designed Gilded Age village where train station, village hall, library, and dining are all within a 0.4-mile radius. Iconic Tudor-style architecture along Pondfield Road.
downtown.verdict: Highest walk score of all 10 markets. Designed for pedestrians from inception — most cohesive walkable village in NYC suburbs. No supermarket within village limits.

research_markets.notes: Best schools of all 10 markets (10/10 GS, 91% math proficiency). Tiny village — 0.6 sq mi, ~6,200 residents. Above budget for SFH. Moderate tax vs. Westchester peers.

research_markets.name: Sea Cliff
research_markets.niche_rank: #75 Best Elementary in NY (Sea Cliff Elem)

downtown.character: Quirky artsy Victorian hillside village with jewel-toned gingerbread houses on winding bluff-top streets above Long Island Sound. Bohemian energy with indie boutiques and a live-music gastropub.
downtown.verdict: Genuinely charming and walkable within its 1 sq mile footprint — unusual for Long Island. LIRR Oyster Bay branch requires Jamaica transfer (65-75 min total) — commute is the primary headwind.

research_markets.notes: Previously removed from primary dashboard. LIRR Oyster Bay branch requires Jamaica transfer — longest commute of all markets. DOM rising sharply (32 to 72 days) — negotiating leverage possible. Strong schools.

research_markets.name: Mamaroneck

downtown.character: Lively harborside village with cafe-lined Mamaroneck Avenue connecting Metro-North station to Long Island Sound. Multicultural main street with authentic diversity and a working harbor marina.
highlights: Harbor Island Park (44 acres on the Sound)
Active waterfront marina with Sound views
downtown.verdict: Genuinely walkable and well-rounded. More vibrant and diverse than Larchmont. Best value play: same A+ schools at ~$550K lower price. Tax trajectory rising sharply is the key risk.

research_markets.notes: Best value play in Westchester — same A+ SD as Larchmont (~$550K lower median). Some inventory $750K-$950K. Tax levy rising: +9.95% in 2025, double-digit increases projected 2026-2027.

research_markets.name: Montclair

downtown.character: Bloomfield Avenue forms a mile-plus spine through four distinct commercial districts — independent bookstores, art galleries, farm-to-table dining, the Wellmont Theater, Montclair Art Museum, and one of NJ's most celebrated coffee scenes. One of the most ethnically diverse suburbs in the entire NYC metro.
highlights: Four walkable commercial districts (Center, Upper, Walnut, Watchung)
downtown.verdict: Richer arts and dining scene than any other market in this set. Car-optional for evenings and weekends — six NJ Transit stations mean most residents walk to the train.

research_markets.notes: Similar lifestyle to Maplewood but larger and more urban. Avg tax bill $22,487 (effective ~2.31% on market value; NJ statutory rate ~3.38% on assessed). School district rated Niche A with diverse academic profile.

research_markets.name: Westfield
research_markets.transit_note: Raritan Valley Line to Newark Penn, then NJT or PATH — no Midtown Direct

downtown.character: Broad Street forms a genuine Main Street with continuous storefronts, sidewalk dining, independent boutiques, and a historic train depot adjacent to the NJ Transit platform. One of the best-preserved traditional downtowns in the NYC metro area.
highlights: Broad Street dining and retail corridor (200+ establishments)
Mindowaskin Park (100-acre green anchor adjacent to downtown)
Westfield train station at the edge of the commercial core
downtown.verdict: One of New Jersey's best Main Streets — station-adjacent, independently-owned mix, and genuine evening foot traffic. The Raritan Valley Line's Newark transfer is the primary commute trade-off vs. Midtown Direct towns like Chatham.

research_markets.notes: Top-ranked Union County district (Niche A+, GS 9/10 — consistently top 5-10% in NJ). Raritan Valley Line requires a Newark Penn transfer adding ~15 min vs. Midtown Direct lines. Price point broadly similar to Maplewood with comparable or better schools. Lower taxes than Essex County (Maplewood, Montclair).

research_markets.name: Chatham

downtown.character: Station-centered Main Street where the NJ Transit Midtown Direct stops steps from T.M. Ward Coffee Co., Crew café, Scalini Fideli, and a tree-lined stretch of local shops. Old-fashioned small-town feel with wide sidewalks and dog-friendly patios — only 2.4 sq mi total.
highlights: Main Street / NJ Transit station (walkable loop)
downtown.verdict: Charming and intimate rather than expansive — more like a true small town than a suburban village strip. Midtown Direct is the key asset: no Secaucus transfer, straight to Penn Station.

research_markets.notes: Morris County taxes are lower than Essex; Chatham SD ranked top-10% in NJ (Niche A+, 97% college placement). Borough vs Township distinction — Borough has the walkable downtown and train station.
